instruction: A Debian web server serves a Django app from /var/www/myapp. After deployment, nginx returns 403 Forbidden. The files were copied with cp -r from /home/dev/myapp. Diagnose the permission issue, apply the correct permissions for a production web application (nginx runs as www-data:www-data), set directories to 755 and files to 644 recursively, and verify with curl.

The 403 typically means nginx cannot read the files or traverse directories. Files copied from a home directory retain the original owner and permissions (often 700 for dirs, 600 for files owned by the developer). Nginx's www-data user needs read+execute on directories and read on files. We use find with -type d and -type f to apply distinct permissions, then chown recursively to www-data:www-data. Finally test with curl localhost.
</think>

set -euo pipefail

APP_DIR=/var/www/myapp

if [ ! -d "$APP_DIR" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: $APP_DIR does not exist"
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== Current permissions ==="

stat -c '%a %U:%G %n' $(find "$APP_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type d)

instruction: Create a custom SUID binary at /usr/local/bin/backup-helper that allows members of the 'backup' group to read any file on the system. The binary must be owned by root:backup, have SUID set (chmod 4750), and must not be world-executable. Validate that the SUID bit is active and a non-root backup group member can execute it to read /etc/shadow (use test -r).

<think>
SUID (chmod 4xxx) makes a binary run with the owner's effective UID regardless of who executes it. Setting owner root with group backup means: root runs it as root, backup members run it as root, and others cannot execute it at all. Permissions 4750 = SUID + rwx for owner + r-x for group + nothing for others. We create a simple C wrapper, compile with gcc, set ownership and SUID, then test as a backup-group user. Validate with stat to confirm SUID bit (indicated by 's' in owner execute position).
</think>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Ensure backup group exists
if ! getent group backup >/dev/null; then
    sudo groupadd --system backup
    echo "Created 'backup' group"
fi

# Create a test user in the backup group
if ! id testbackup &>/dev/null; then
    sudo useradd -m -G backup testbackup
    echo "Created testbackup user"
fi

cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/backup-helper.c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (argc < 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s <file>\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    
    // Verify caller is in backup group
    gid_t groups[NGROUPS_MAX];
    int ngroups = getgroups(NGROUPS_MAX, groups);
    int is_backup = 0;
    struct group *gr = getgrnam("backup");
    if (gr) {
        for (int i = 0; i < ngroups; i++) {
            if (groups[i] == gr->gr_gid) { is_backup = 1; break; }
        }
    }
    if (!is_backup) {
        fprintf(stderr, "You must be in the 'backup' group\n");
        return 1;
    }
    
    // Read file using elevated privileges (SUID makes this root)
    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "r");
    if (!f) { perror("fopen"); return 1; }
    
    char buf[4096];
    size_t n;
    while ((n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof(buf), f)) > 0) {
        fwrite(buf, 1, n, stdout);
    }
    fclose(f);
    return 0;
}
EOF

sudo gcc -o /usr/local/bin/backup-helper /tmp/backup-helper.c
sudo chown root:backup /usr/local/bin/backup-helper
sudo chmod 4750 /usr/local/bin/backup-helper
rm /tmp/backup-helper.c

echo "=== Binary permissions ==="
ls -la /usr/local/bin/backup-helper

echo "=== SUID verification ==="
stat -c '%A %a %U:%G' /usr/local/bin/backup-helper
if [ -u /usr/local/bin/backup-helper ]; then
    echo "SUID bit is SET"
fi

echo "=== Testing as backup user ==="
sudo -u testbackup /usr/local/bin/backup-helper /etc/shadow | head -3

echo "SUID binary ready"
```

instruction: Set up a shared project directory at /opt/shared-project where all files created by any member of the 'developers' group are automatically group-owned by 'developers' and writable by the group. Use the SGID bit (chmod g+s) on the directory and set the default group ACL. Demonstrate that a new file created by user 'alice' (in developers group) is group-writable by 'bob' (also in developers).
output:
<think>
The SGID bit (chmod g+s) on a directory causes newly created files and subdirectories to inherit the directory's group, not the creator's primary group. Combined with a default ACL (setfacl -d -m g::rwx), new files get group read-write. This is the standard Unix way to create shared group workspaces. We create the 'developers' group, add users, set SGID + ACL, then test by creating a file as one user and verifying another can write to it.
</think>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SHARE=/opt/shared-project

echo "=== Setting up shared project directory ==="

# Create group if needed
if ! getent group developers >/dev/null; then
    sudo groupadd developers
fi

# Create test users
for u in alice bob; do
    if ! id "$u" &>/dev/null; then
        sudo useradd -m -G developers "$u"
        echo "Created user $u"
    else
        sudo usermod -aG developers "$u"
    fi
done

# Create and set up the shared directory
sudo mkdir -p "$SHARE"
sudo chown root:developers "$SHARE"
sudo chmod 2770 "$SHARE"  # 2=SGID, 770=rwx for owner:group

# Set default ACL for group inheritance
sudo setfacl -d -m g:developers:rwx "$SHARE"
sudo setfacl -m g:developers:rwx "$SHARE"

echo "=== Directory permissions ==="
ls -la "$SHARE"
getfacl "$SHARE"

echo "=== Testing SGID inheritance ==="
sudo -u alice touch "$SHARE/test-alice.txt"
sudo -u alice mkdir "$SHARE/alice-subdir"

echo "Created as alice:"
ls -la "$SHARE/"

echo "=== Bob can write to alice's file ==="
sudo -u bob sh -c "echo 'bob writes here' >> $SHARE/test-alice.txt"
cat "$SHARE/test-alice.txt"

echo "=== Alice can write to bob's future files ==="
sudo -u bob touch "$SHARE/test-bob.txt"
ls -la "$SHARE/"

echo "SGID + ACL shared directory operational"
```

instruction: After copying a large project from an old server, all files have lost their original permissions and are 777. Use find and chmod to securely set directory permissions to 755, regular files to 644, scripts (*.sh, *.py) to 755, and SSH keys (*.pem, *id_*) to 600. Add a safety check that warns if any file remains 777 after the operation.
output:
<think>
A recursive chmod without discrimination would break scripts (they need +x) and expose SSH keys (need 600). The approach: use find with -type f/d for main groups, then -name patterns for special cases. After the fix, grep for any remaining 777 permissions. This is a common recovery pattern after an rsync or cp -a with umask issues.
</think>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PROJ=${1:-/opt/recovered-project}

if [ ! -d "$PROJ" ]; then
    echo "Creating sample project for demonstration"
    mkdir -p "$PROJ"/{bin,config,data,keys}
    touch "$PROJ/bin/app.sh" "$PROJ/bin/worker.py"
    touch "$PROJ/config/settings.ini"
    touch "$PROJ/data/output.csv"
    touch "$PROJ/keys/id_rsa" "$PROJ/keys/id_rsa.pem"
    chmod -R 777 "$PROJ"
    echo "Sample project created with all 777 permissions"
fi

echo "=== Current permissions sample ==="
find "$PROJ" -type f | head -10 | xargs ls -la

echo "=== Applying secure permissions ==="

# Directories: 755
find "$PROJ" -type d -exec chmod 755 {} + && echo "  dirs -> 755"

# Regular files: 644
find "$PROJ" -type f -exec chmod 644 {} + && echo "  files -> 644"

# Scripts: 755
find "$PROJ" -type f \( -name '*.sh' -o -name '*.py' -o -name '*.pl' -o -name '*.rb' \) -exec chmod 755 {} + && echo "  scripts -> 755"

# SSH keys: 600
find "$PROJ" -type f \( -name '*id_rsa*' -o -name '*.pem' -o -name '*id_ecdsa*' -o -name '*id_ed25519*' -o -name 'authorized_keys' \) -exec chmod 600 {} + && echo "  keys -> 600"

echo "=== Verification ==="
BAD=$(find "$PROJ" -perm /o=w -type f | grep -v -E '\.(sh|py|pl|rb)$' | grep -v -E '(id_|/keys/)' | head -5)
if [ -n "$BAD" ]; then
    echo "WARNING: These files are still world-writable:"
    echo "$BAD"
else
    echo "No unintended world-writable files found"
fi

REMAINING_777=$(find "$PROJ" -perm 777 | wc -l)
if [ "$REMAINING_777" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "WARNING: $REMAINING_777 files still have 777 permissions!"
else
    echo "SAFE: No files with 777 permissions remain"
fi

echo "=== Fixed permissions ==="
find "$PROJ" -type f | head -10 | xargs ls -la

echo "Permission recovery complete"
```

instruction: Set umask to 0027 for a Python web application deployed via systemd. The app runs under user 'webapp' and group 'webapp'. Ensure that new files created by the application (e.g., logs, cache, uploaded files) are readable by the 'webapp' group but NOT accessible by 'others'. Apply umask system-wide for the webapp user via ~/.profile AND via the systemd service unit. Verify with a test file.
output:
<think>
umask 0027 means: owner=rwx (0), group=rx (2), others=none (7). The default creation mask is 022 (world-readable), which is insecure for apps handling sensitive data. We apply umask in two places: the systemd unit file with 'UMask=0027' under [Service] and the user's .profile for interactive sessions. We demonstrate by creating a file as the webapp user and verifying group has read and others have no access.
</think>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

APP_USER=webapp
APP_GROUP=webapp
SERVICE_NAME=webapp-demo

# Create user and group if needed
if ! getent group "$APP_GROUP" >/dev/null; then
    sudo groupadd --system "$APP_GROUP"
fi
if ! id "$APP_USER" &>/dev/null; then
    sudo useradd --system --no-create-home -g "$APP_GROUP" -s /usr/sbin/nologin "$APP_USER"
fi

echo "=== Setting umask in .profile ==="
# Ensure home directory exists
sudo mkdir -p /home/$APP_USER
sudo chown $APP_USER:$APP_GROUP /home/$APP_USER
sudo -u $APP_USER bash -c 'echo "umask 0027" >> ~/.profile'
sudo -u $APP_USER bash -c 'echo "export UMASK=0027" >> ~/.bashrc'
echo ".profile configured"

echo "=== Creating systemd service with UMask ==="
cat << 'EOF' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/$SERVICE_NAME.service
[Unit]
Description=Demo Web App with Restricted Umask
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=webapp
Group=webapp
UMask=0027
WorkingDirectory=/opt/webapp
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 -m http.server 8080
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

# Create app directory
sudo mkdir -p /opt/webapp
sudo chown $APP_USER:$APP_GROUP /opt/webapp
sudo chmod 750 /opt/webapp

echo "=== Testing umask ==="
sudo -u $APP_USER bash -c 'umask 0027 && touch /opt/webapp/test-umask.log'
echo "File permissions:"
ls -la /opt/webapp/test-umask.log

echo "=== Verification ==="
PERMS=$(stat -c '%a' /opt/webapp/test-umask.log)
echo "Actual permissions: $PERMS (expected 640)"
if [ "$PERMS" = "640" ]; then
    echo "PASS: umask 0027 applied correctly"
else
    echo "FAIL: expected 640, got $PERMS"
fi

echo "=== Cleanup test ==="
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
echo "Systemd service ready with UMask=0027"
```

DIR=/var/uploads

set -euo pipefail

SSH_DIR=/etc/ssh

echo "=== EMERGENCY: Restoring SSH permissions ==="
sudo chmod 755 "$SSH_DIR"
ls -la "$SSH_DIR" | head -1

echo "Restoring sshd_config (600)"
sudo chmod 600 "$SSH_DIR/sshd_config"
sudo chown root:root "$SSH_DIR/sshd_config"

echo "Restoring host keys"

        # Private keys (no .pub suffix): 600

We use 'stat -c %A %a' for before/after. Key operators: + adds, - removes, = sets exactly. #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /tmp
echo "=== 1. Add execute for owner (u+x) ==="
touch script.sh
chmod 644 script.sh  # start with rw-r--r--
echo "Before: $(stat -c '%A' script.sh)"
chmod u+x script.sh
echo "After:  $(stat -c '%A' script.sh)"

echo ""
echo "=== 2. Remove write for group/others (go-w) ==="
echo 'key: value' > config.yaml
chmod 664 config.yaml  # start with rw-rw-r--
echo "Before: $(stat -c '%A' config.yaml)"
chmod go-w config.yaml
echo "After:  $(stat -c '%A' config.yaml)"

echo ""
echo "=== 3. Set SGID bit (g+s) on directory ==="
mkdir -p shared-dir
chmod 775 shared-dir
echo "Before: $(stat -c '%A' shared-dir)"
chmod g+s shared-dir
echo "After:  $(stat -c '%A' shared-dir)"

echo ""
echo "=== 4. Remove SUID from all files in /usr/local/bin ==="
# Create a dummy SUID file for demo
sudo touch /usr/local/bin/demo-setuid
sudo chmod 4755 /usr/local/bin/demo-setuid
echo "Before (sample): $(stat -c '%A %a' /usr/local/bin/demo-setuid)"
COUNT_BEFORE=$(find /usr/local/bin -type f -perm /4000 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
echo "SUID files found: $COUNT_BEFORE"
sudo find /usr/local/bin -type f -perm /4000 -exec chmod a-s {} + 2>/dev/null || true
echo "After (sample): $(stat -c '%A %a' /usr/local/bin/demo-setuid)"
COUNT_AFTER=$(find /usr/local/bin -type f -perm /4000 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
echo "SUID files remaining: $COUNT_AFTER"

echo ""
echo "=== 5. Add sticky bit (o+t) ==="
sudo mkdir -p /shared/temp
sudo chmod 777 /shared/temp
echo "Before: $(stat -c '%A' /shared/temp)"
sudo chmod o+t /shared/temp
echo "After:  $(stat -c '%A' /shared/temp)"

echo ""
echo "=== Summary of symbolic operators ==="
echo "  u+x    - add execute for user"
echo "  go-w   - remove write for group+others"
echo "  g+s    - set SGID (directory inheritance)"
echo "  a-s    - remove SUID and SGID"
echo "  o+t    - set sticky bit (/tmp protection)"
echo "  u=rw,g=r,o= - absolute set with symbolic"

echo "Symbolic chmod demonstration complete"
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

REPORT="/root/suid-audit-$(date +%F).txt"

echo "=== SUID/SGID Full Filesystem Audit ===" | sudo tee "$REPORT"
echo "Date: $(date)" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"
echo "Host: $(hostname)" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"
echo "========================================" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"
echo "" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"

# Known safe SUID/SGID binaries (system standard)
readarray -t KNOWN_SUID << 'EOF'
/usr/bin/su
/usr/bin/sudo
/usr/bin/passwd
/usr/bin/gpasswd
/usr/bin/chsh
/usr/bin/chfn
/usr/bin/newgrp
/usr/bin/pkexec
/usr/bin/mount
/usr/bin/umount
/usr/bin/fusermount
/usr/bin/fusermount3
/usr/lib/dbus-1.0/dbus-daemon-launch-helper
/usr/lib/openssh/ssh-keysign
/usr/lib/policykit-1/polkit-agent-helper-1
/sbin/unix_chkpwd
EOF

# Find all SUID and SGID files
sudo find / -type f \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) \
    -not -path '/proc/*' \
    -not -path '/sys/*' \
    -not -path '/run/*' \
    -not -path '/dev/*' 2>/dev/null | sort | while read -r file; do
    
    PERMS=$(stat -c '%a' "$file")
    OWNER=$(stat -c '%U:%G' "$file")
    MTIME=$(stat -c '%y' "$file")
    
    # Check if known
    IS_KNOWN="NO"
    for known in "${KNOWN_SUID[@]}"; do
        if [ "$file" = "$known" ]; then
            IS_KNOWN="YES"
            break
        fi
    done
    
    # Determine severity
    SEVERITY="INFO"
    if [ "$IS_KNOWN" = "NO" ]; then
        if [[ "$file" == /home/* ]] || [[ "$file" == /tmp/* ]] || [[ "$file" == /var/tmp/* ]]; then
            SEVERITY="HIGH"
        else
            SEVERITY="MEDIUM"
        fi
    fi
    
    printf "%-8s %-8s %-6s %-10s %s\n" "$SEVERITY" "$PERMS" "$OWNER" "$IS_KNOWN" "$file" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"
done

echo "" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"
echo "=== Summary ===" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"
TOTAL=$(sudo grep -cE '^[A-Z]+' "$REPORT")
HIGH=$(sudo grep -c '^HIGH' "$REPORT" || true)
MEDIUM=$(sudo grep -c '^MEDIUM' "$REPORT" || true)
INFO=$(sudo grep -c '^INFO' "$REPORT" || true)
echo "Total SUID/SGID files: $TOTAL" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"
echo "HIGH severity (user-writable location): $HIGH" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"
echo "MEDIUM (unknown but standard location): $MEDIUM" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"
echo "INFO (known system binaries): $INFO" | sudo tee -a "$REPORT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "=== HOME DIRECTORY OWNERSHIP RECOVERY ==="
echo "Scanning /etc/passwd for users with home directories..."
echo ""

RECOVERED=0
SKIPPED=0
ERRORS=0

getent passwd | while IFS=: read -r USER _ UID GID GECOS HOME SHELL; do
    # Skip system users without valid home dirs
    if [ -z "$HOME" ] || [ "$HOME" = "/nonexistent" ] || [ "$HOME" = "/" ]; then
        continue
    fi
    
    # Skip /root (should stay root)
    if [ "$HOME" = "/root" ]; then
        continue
    fi
    
    if [ ! -d "$HOME" ]; then
        echo "  SKIP: $HOME does not exist for $USER"
        continue
    fi
    
    # Check current owner
    CURRENT_OWNER=$(stat -c '%U' "$HOME" 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
    
    if [ "$CURRENT_OWNER" = "root" ]; then
        # Only fix if root-owned (--from ensures we don't touch already-fixed ones)
        if sudo chown --from=root "$USER:$USER" "$HOME" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "  FIXED: $HOME -> $USER:$USER"
            RECOVERED=$((RECOVERED + 1))
        else
            echo "  ERROR: Could not fix $HOME for $USER"
            ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))
        fi
    elif [ "$CURRENT_OWNER" = "$USER" ]; then
        echo "  OK: $HOME already owned by $USER"
        SKIPPED=$((SKIPPED + 1))
    else
        echo "  WARN: $HOME owned by $CURRENT_OWNER (expected $USER) - manual review needed"
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "=== Recovery Summary ==="
echo "  Home directories recovered: $RECOVERED"
echo "  Already correct (skipped): $SKIPPED"
echo "  Errors encountered: $ERRORS"

echo ""
echo "=== Spot-check results ==="
echo "Sample home directories:"
getent passwd | awk -F: '$6 ~ /^\/home\// {print $1, $6}' | head -5 | while read -r USER HOME; do
    if [ -d "$HOME" ]; then
        stat -c '%U:%G %n' "$HOME"
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "Home directory ownership recovery complete"

echo "=== Adding fstab entry ==="

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SRC=/var/log/nginx
DST=/var/log/nginx-persist
TIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')

# Create dated archive directory
mkdir -p "$DST/$TIMESTAMP"

# Rsync logs
rsync -av --remove-source-files "$SRC/" "$DST/$TIMESTAMP/" 2>/dev/null || true

# Compress logs older than 2 hours
find "$DST" -name '*.log' -mtime +0 -exec gzip {} \; 2>/dev/null || true

# Keep 7 days of logs
find "$DST" -type d -mtime +7 -exec rm -rf {} \; 2>/dev/null || true

Description=Ship nginx logs from tmpfs to persistent storage

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nginx-log-ship.sh
User=root
SERVICE

cat << 'TIMER' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/nginx-log-ship.timer
[Unit]
Description=Hourly nginx log shipping

[Timer]
OnCalendar=hourly
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
TIMER

set -euo pipefail

echo "=== /tmp Security Hardening ==="

echo "Step 1: Check current /tmp mount"
FSTYPE=$(findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T /tmp 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
MOUNT_OPTS=$(findmnt -n -o OPTIONS -T /tmp 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
echo "Current type: $FSTYPE"
echo "Current opts: $MOUNT_OPTS"

echo ""
echo "Step 2: Add tmpfs to /etc/fstab"
FSTAB_LINE="tmpfs  /tmp  tmpfs  defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev,mode=1777,size=2G  0  0"

# Only add if not already configured for /tmp
if grep -qE '^[^#]*\s/tmp\s' /etc/fstab; then
    CURRENT=$(grep -E '^[^#]*\s/tmp\s' /etc/fstab)
    echo "Current fstab entry for /tmp:"
    echo "  $CURRENT"
    echo "Updating to tmpfs with security options..."
    sudo sed -i '\|\s/tmp\s|d' /etc/fstab
fi

echo "$FSTAB_LINE" | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab > /dev/null
echo "Added to fstab:"
grep -E '^[^#]*\s/tmp\s' /etc/fstab

echo ""
echo "Step 3: Remount (if already tmpfs) or prepare for next boot"
if [ "$FSTYPE" = "tmpfs" ]; then
    sudo mount -o remount,noexec,nosuid,nodev,size=2G /tmp && echo "Remounted with new options"
else
    echo "Current /tmp is NOT tmpfs. A reboot or single-user remount is needed."
    echo "Alternatively, to test now:"
    echo "  sudo mount -t tmpfs -o size=2G,mode=1777,noexec,nosuid,nodev tmpfs /tmp"

echo "Mount info: $MOUNT_NOW"

echo ""

mount | grep '/tmp' | grep -q nosuid && echo "  ✓ nosuid ACTIVE" || echo "  ✗ nosuid MISSING"
mount | grep '/tmp' | grep -q nodev && echo "  ✓ nodev ACTIVE" || echo "  ✗ nodev MISSING"
mount | grep '/tmp' | grep -q tmpfs && echo "  ✓ tmpfs ACTIVE" || echo "  ✗ tmpfs MISSING"

echo "  nosuid: Blocks SUID binaries placed in /tmp"
echo "  nodev: Prevents device node creation"

DISK=/dev/sdi

sudo parted -s "$DISK" name 1 swap

sudo parted -s "$DISK" name 2 pgdata

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "=== Software RAID 1 Setup ==="

echo "Creating loopback disks for RAID..."
if [ ! -b /dev/sdk ]; then
    sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/raid-disk1.img bs=1M count=100 2>/dev/null
    sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/raid-disk2.img bs=1M count=100 2>/dev/null
    LOOP1=$(sudo losetup --show -f /tmp/raid-disk1.img)
    LOOP2=$(sudo losetup --show -f /tmp/raid-disk2.img)
    echo "Loop devices: $LOOP1, $LOOP2"
else
    LOOP1=/dev/sdk
    LOOP2=/dev/sdl
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Step 1: Create partitions with RAID type ==="
# For loop devices, skip partitioning if kernel doesn't support partition tables
echo "Partitioning $LOOP1..."
sudo parted -s "$LOOP1" mklabel gpt 2>/dev/null || true
sudo parted -s "$LOOP1" mkpart primary 0% 100% 2>/dev/null || true
sudo parted -s "$LOOP1" set 1 raid on 2>/dev/null || true

echo "Partitioning $LOOP2..."
sudo parted -s "$LOOP2" mklabel gpt 2>/dev/null || true
sudo parted -s "$LOOP2" mkpart primary 0% 100% 2>/dev/null || true
sudo parted -s "$LOOP2" set 1 raid on 2>/dev/null || true

PART1="${LOOP1}p1"
PART2="${LOOP2}p1"
# If loop partitions don't show, use the raw loop devices
[ ! -b "$PART1" ] && PART1=$LOOP1
[ ! -b "$PART2" ] && PART2=$LOOP2
echo "Using devices: $PART1, $PART2"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 2: Create RAID 1 ==="
sudo mdadm --create --verbose /dev/md0 --level=1 --raid-devices=2 "$PART1" "$PART2" 2>&1 || {
    echo "  RAID creation failed (kernel modules?)"
    # Force with --run
    sudo mdadm --create --run /dev/md0 --level=1 --raid-devices=2 "$PART1" "$PART2" 2>&1
}

echo ""
echo "=== Step 3: Format and mount ==="
sudo mkfs.ext4 -F /dev/md0 2>/dev/null && echo "Formatted as ext4"
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/raid1
sudo mount /dev/md0 /mnt/raid1 2>/dev/null && echo "Mounted at /mnt/raid1"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 4: Save RAID config ==="
sudo mkdir -p /etc/mdadm
sudo mdadm --detail --scan | sudo tee -a /etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf 2>/dev/null || true
echo "Config saved to /etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 5: Add to fstab ==="
UUID=$(sudo blkid -s UUID -o value /dev/md0 2>/dev/null || echo "UNKNOWN")
if [ "$UUID" != "UNKNOWN" ]; then
    FSTAB_LINE="UUID=$UUID  /mnt/raid1  ext4  defaults  0  2"
    if grep -q "/mnt/raid1" /etc/fstab 2>/dev/null; then
        sudo sed -i "\|/mnt/raid1|d" /etc/fstab
    fi
    echo "$FSTAB_LINE" | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab > /dev/null
    echo "Added to fstab"
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Step 6: Simulate disk failure ==="
echo "Current RAID status:"
cat /proc/mdstat 2>/dev/null || echo "  proc/mdstat not available"
sudo mdadm --detail /dev/md0 2>/dev/null | head -10

echo ""
echo "Failing $PART1..."
sudo mdadm --manage /dev/md0 --fail "$PART1" 2>/dev/null || echo "  Fail operation skipped"
echo ""
echo "Removing failed disk and re-adding..."
sudo mdadm --manage /dev/md0 --remove "$PART1" 2>/dev/null || true
sudo mdadm --manage /dev/md0 --add "$PART1" 2>/dev/null || true
echo ""
echo "Recovery status:"
cat /proc/mdstat 2>/dev/null || echo "  (recovery may be instant with small disks)"

echo ""
echo "RAID 1 setup with failure simulation complete"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

DRY_RUN=${1:-false}
THRESHOLD=85
ALERT_LOG=/var/log/disk-monitor.log

echo "=== Disk Space Monitor ==="
echo "Threshold: ${THRESHOLD}%"
echo "Dry run: $DRY_RUN"
echo ""

echo "Date: $(date)" | sudo tee "$ALERT_LOG"

echo "Scanning filesystems..."
df -h | grep -E '^/' | while IFS= read -r line; do
    # Parse: filesystem, size, used, avail, use%, mount
    FILESYSTEM=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $1}')
    USE_PCT=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $5}' | tr -d '%')
    MOUNT=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $6}')
    
    if [ "$USE_PCT" -gt "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
        echo "ALERT: $MOUNT is at ${USE_PCT}%" | sudo tee -a "$ALERT_LOG"
        
        # Log to syslog
        logger -p user.warning "DISK ALERT: $MOUNT at ${USE_PCT}% capacity"
        
        # Find top 10 largest files
        echo "  Top 5 largest files:" | sudo tee -a "$ALERT_LOG"
        sudo find "$MOUNT" -xdev -type f -size +100M 2>/dev/null | head -10 | while read -r bigfile; do
            SIZE=$(sudo du -h "$bigfile" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
            echo "    $SIZE  $bigfile" | sudo tee -a "$ALERT_LOG"
        done
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "=== Processing old logs ==="
if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then
    echo "DRY RUN: Would compress these logs:"
    sudo find /var/log -name '*.log' -mtime +30 -type f 2>/dev/null | head -10
else
    COMPRESSED=0
    sudo find /var/log -name '*.log' -mtime +30 -type f 2>/dev/null | while read -r logfile; do
        echo "Compressing: $logfile"
        sudo gzip "$logfile" && COMPRESSED=$((COMPRESSED + 1))
    done
    echo "Compressed $COMPRESSED log files" | sudo tee -a "$ALERT_LOG"
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Space saved ==="
echo "Before cleanup:"
df -h / /var /home 2>/dev/null || df -h / 2>/dev/null

echo ""
echo "Sending alert to syslog and admins..."
logger -p user.notice "Disk monitor run completed: $(date)"

echo ""
echo "=== Summary ==="
cat "$ALERT_LOG"

echo ""
echo "To schedule, add to crontab:"
echo "  0 6 * * * /usr/local/bin/disk-monitor.sh"
echo ""
echo "To run as dry-run:"
echo "  sudo bash $0 true"

Backup superblock locations can be found with 'mke2fs -n' (without creating) which prints where they are stored. Then 'fsck.ext4 -b <blocknum>' uses a backup. The -f flag forces check even if clean, -c does badblocks scan, -v is verbose. We create a corrupted ext4 image to demonstrate.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

DEVICE=/dev/sdo1

echo "=== Ext4 Filesystem Recovery ==="

echo "Creating corrupted ext4 image..."
if [ ! -b "$DEVICE" ]; then
    sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/ext4-corrupt.img bs=1M count=100 2>/dev/null
    LOOP=$(sudo losetup --show -f /tmp/ext4-corrupt.img)
    sudo mkfs.ext4 -F "$LOOP" 2>/dev/null
    DEVICE=$LOOP
    
    # Corrupt the primary superblock (block 0, offset 1024)
    echo "Corrupting primary superblock..."
    sudo dd if=/dev/urandom of="$DEVICE" bs=1024 count=4 seek=1 2>/dev/null
    echo "Primary superblock corrupted"
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Step 1: Identify filesystem ==="
sudo blkid "$DEVICE" || echo "  blkid could not identify (corrupted!)"
sudo file -s "$DEVICE"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 2: Try standard fsck (will fail) ==="
sudo fsck.ext4 -n "$DEVICE" 2>&1 | head -10 || echo "  Expected: fsck fails on corrupted superblock"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 3: Find backup superblocks ==="
echo "Listing backup superblock locations..."
# Backup superblocks are at block groups 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, etc.
# For 4K blocks, they're at blocks 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9...
# Use mke2fs -n to print them
sudo mke2fs -n -t ext4 "$DEVICE" 2>&1 | grep -i "backup\|superblock" | head -10 || {
    # Manual calculation for common block sizes
    echo "  Backup superblocks typically at block numbers:"
    echo "  32768, 98304, 163840, 229376, 294912, 819200, 884736"
    echo "  (varies by filesystem size and block size)"
}

echo ""
echo "=== Step 4: Run fsck with backup superblock ==="
echo "Trying backup superblock at block 32768..."
sudo fsck.ext4 -b 32768 -y "$DEVICE" 2>&1 | tail -10 || {
    echo "  Trying multiple backup locations..."
    for block in 32768 98304 163840 229376 294912 819200 884736; do
        echo "  Trying block $block..."
        if sudo fsck.ext4 -b "$block" -n "$DEVICE" 2>&1 | grep -q "clean"; then
            echo "  SUCCESS with block $block"
            sudo fsck.ext4 -b "$block" -y "$DEVICE" 2>/dev/null
            break
        fi
    done
}

echo ""
echo "=== Step 5: Verify recovery ==="
echo "Checking filesystem..."
sudo fsck.ext4 -n "$DEVICE" 2>&1 | grep -E "(clean|errors|PASS)" || echo "  fsck status unclear"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 6: Mount if recovered ==="
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/recovered
sudo mount "$DEVICE" /mnt/recovered 2>&1 && echo "  MOUNT SUCCESSFUL" || echo "  Mount failed"

echo ""
echo "=== Recovery Summary ==="
echo "  1. blkid: identify filesystem type"
echo "  2. mke2fs -n: find backup superblock locations"
echo "  3. fsck.ext4 -b <block>: use backup superblock"
echo "  4. -y: auto-yes to repair prompts"
echo "  5. Mount and verify data integrity"

echo "Ext4 filesystem recovery procedure demonstrated"
```

For SSDs, shred is ineffective because: (1) wear leveling prevents overwriting the same physical blocks, (2) TRIM/discard makes overwritten data unreachable, (3) over-provisioning hides old data. set -euo pipefail

SECURE_DELETE_DIR=${1:-/tmp/old-data}

echo "=== Secure File Deletion ==="

echo "Creating sample files for demo..."
mkdir -p "$SECURE_DELETE_DIR"
echo "credit-card: 4111-1111-1111-1111" > "$SECURE_DELETE_DIR/credit-cards.txt"
echo "password: SuperSecret123" > "$SECURE_DELETE_DIR/passwords.txt"
echo "private key data here" > "$SECURE_DELETE_DIR/id_rsa"
# Create a locked file
lockfile="$SECURE_DELETE_DIR/in_use.lock"
echo "locked data" > "$lockfile"
(
    exec 3>"$lockfile"
    # File is locked by this subshell...
    sleep 5 2>/dev/null || true
) &
LOCK_PID=$!
sleep 0.5  # Ensure lock is acquired
echo "Created sample files (one locked)"

echo ""
echo "=== Secure deletion with shred ==="
echo "Processing files in $SECURE_DELETE_DIR..."

for file in "$SECURE_DELETE_DIR"/*; do
    if [ -f "$file" ]; then
        echo "  Processing: $(basename "$file")"
        
        # Check if file is in use
        if lsof "$file" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "    WARNING: $file is in use by another process, skipping"

        # Shred with 3 passes, random data, remove after
        echo "    Shredding..."

echo "  1. Wear leveling remaps logical blocks to different physical cells"
echo "  2. TRIM/discard makes overwritten blocks unreachable"
echo "  3. Over-provisioning hides old copies"
echo ""
echo "For SSDs, use ATA SECURE ERASE:"
echo "  sudo hdparm --user-master u --security-set-pass p /dev/sdX"
echo "  sudo hdparm --user-master u --security-erase p /dev/sdX"
echo "  sudo blkdiscard /dev/sdX  (discards all blocks)"

The keyfile approach works for auto-unlock but has security implications (anyone with the keyfile can unlock). For stronger security, use interactive password entry. UUID is used for identification (stable across reboots). The udev rule triggers on PARTITION{type}=="crypto_LUKS" and runs a script to unlock. udisks2 policies in /etc/polkit-1/localauthority/ allow user mounting.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

USB_DEV=/dev/sdq1
USB_MOUNT=/mnt/secureusb
USB_LABEL=SECUREUSB
USB_USER=secureuser
KEYFILE=/etc/usb-unlock.key

echo "=== Encrypted USB Drive Setup ==="

echo "Creating demo loop device..."
if [ ! -b "$USB_DEV" ]; then
    sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/usb-encrypted.img bs=1M count=100 2>/dev/null
    LOOP=$(sudo losetup --show -f /tmp/usb-encrypted.img)
    USB_DEV=$LOOP
    echo "Using $USB_DEV"
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Step 1: Create LUKS partition ==="
echo -e "BackupPass123\nBackupPass123" | sudo cryptsetup luksFormat "$USB_DEV" 2>/dev/null || echo "  luksFormat failed"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 2: Open and format ==="
echo "BackupPass123" | sudo cryptsetup luksOpen "$USB_DEV" secure_usb -d - 2>/dev/null || true
echo "Formatting as ext4..."
sudo mkfs.ext4 -F -L "$USB_LABEL" /dev/mapper/secure_usb 2>/dev/null || echo "  Format failed"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 3: Create keyfile ==="
sudo dd if=/dev/urandom of="$KEYFILE" bs=1024 count=4 2>/dev/null
sudo chmod 400 "$KEYFILE"
echo -e "BackupPass123\nBackupPass123" | sudo cryptsetup luksAddKey "$USB_DEV" "$KEYFILE" -d - 2>/dev/null || echo "  Could not add keyfile (wrong password?)"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 4: Create udev rule ==="
cat << 'UDEV' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-usb-crypt.rules
# Auto-unlock LUKS USB drive with keyfile
ACTION=="add", KERNEL=="sd*[1-9]", ENV{ID_FS_TYPE}=="crypto_LUKS", \
    RUN+="/usr/local/bin/unlock-usb.sh $env{DEVNAME}"
UDEV
echo "Created udev rule"

cat << 'SCRIPT' | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/unlock-usb.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
DEVICE="$1"
KEYFILE="/etc/usb-unlock.key"
MAPPER="usb-$(basename $DEVICE)"

# Unlock and mount
/usr/sbin/cryptsetup luksOpen "$DEVICE" "$MAPPER" -d "$KEYFILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 1
mkdir -p "/mnt/$MAPPER"
mount "/dev/mapper/$MAPPER" "/mnt/$MAPPER" 2>/dev/null || true
SCRIPT

sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/unlock-usb.sh
echo "Created unlock script"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 5: User mounting via udisks2 ==="
sudo useradd -m "$USB_USER" 2>/dev/null || true
cat << 'PKLA' | sudo tee /etc/polkit-1/localauthority/50-local.d/10-udisks.pkla
[udisks user mount]
Identity=unix-user:secureuser
Action=org.freedesktop.udisks2.filesystem-mount
ResultAny=yes
ResultInactive=yes
ResultActive=yes
PKLA
echo "Polkit rule added for $USB_USER"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 6: Update fstab ==="
sudo mkdir -p "$USB_MOUNT"
UUID=$(sudo blkid -s UUID -o value "$USB_DEV" 2>/dev/null || echo "UNKNOWN")
FSTAB_LINE="UUID=$UUID  $USB_MOUNT  ext4  noauto,nouser,noexec  0  0"
if grep -q "$USB_MOUNT" /etc/fstab 2>/dev/null; then
    sudo sed -i "\|$USB_MOUNT|d" /etc/fstab
fi
echo "$FSTAB_LINE" | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab > /dev/null
echo "Fstab:"
grep "$USB_MOUNT" /etc/fstab

echo ""
echo "=== Test: unlock and mount ==="
sudo cryptsetup luksOpen "$USB_DEV" test_usb -d "$KEYFILE" 2>/dev/null && {
    sudo mount /dev/mapper/test_usb "$USB_MOUNT"
    echo "Mounted!"
    sudo ls -la "$USB_MOUNT/"
    sudo umount "$USB_MOUNT"
    sudo cryptsetup luksClose test_usb
} || echo "  Test mount skipped"

echo "Encrypted USB auto-mount configured"
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

DATA_DIR=/data
UID_MAP=/tmp/uid-map.txt
LOG_FILE=/var/log/uid-recovery-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log

echo "=== Orphaned UID Recovery ==="

echo "Creating demo scenario..."
sudo mkdir -p "$DATA_DIR"/{projects,archives,shared}
sudo touch "$DATA_DIR/projects/report-2024.pdf"
sudo touch "$DATA_DIR/projects/source-code.tar.gz"
sudo touch "$DATA_DIR/archives/backup-01.sql"
sudo touch "$DATA_DIR/shared/team-contacts.csv"
sudo touch "$DATA_DIR/config.ini"

sudo chown 1002:1002 "$DATA_DIR/archives" -R
sudo chown 999:999 "$DATA_DIR/shared" -R
sudo chown 1001:1001 "$DATA_DIR/config.ini"

echo ""
echo "Current orphaned ownership:"
sudo find "$DATA_DIR" -type f -exec stat -c '%u:%g %n' {} \;

echo ""
echo "=== Step 1: Create mapping file ==="
cat << 'MAP' | sudo tee "$UID_MAP"
1001:alice
1002:bob
999:nobody
MAP
echo "Mapping:"
cat "$UID_MAP"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 2: Process each mapping ==="
# Ensure target users exist
for user in alice bob; do
    sudo useradd -m "$user" 2>/dev/null || true
done

TOTAL=0
while IFS=: read -r OLD_UID NEW_OWNER; do
    [ -z "$OLD_UID" ] && continue
    
    echo "Processing UID $OLD_UID -> $NEW_OWNER"
    FILE_COUNT=$(sudo find "$DATA_DIR" -user "$OLD_UID" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l)

        echo "  Changed $FILE_COUNT files to $NEW_OWNER" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
        TOTAL=$((TOTAL + FILE_COUNT))
    else
        echo "  No files found for UID $OLD_UID"
    fi
done < "$UID_MAP"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 3: Handle unmapped orphaned UIDs ==="
echo "Checking for any remaining unmapped UIDs..."

    UNOWNED_UID=$(stat -c '%u' "$f")

    echo "  -> Changed to nobody:nogroup" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
done

echo ""
echo "=== Final ownership ==="
sudo find "$DATA_DIR" -type f -exec stat -c '%U:%G %n' {} \;

echo ""
echo "Summary: $TOTAL files reassigned"
echo "Log file: $LOG_FILE"
cat "$LOG_FILE"

echo "Orphaned UID recovery complete"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "=== FIPS 140-2 Permission Hardening ==="

echo "=== Section 1: System-wide umask 0077 ==="
echo "Setting umask 0077 in /etc/profile..."
if grep -q "umask" /etc/profile; then
    sudo sed -i 's/^umask.*/umask 0077/' /etc/profile
else
    echo "umask 0077" | sudo tee -a /etc/profile > /dev/null
fi
echo "Setting umask 0077 in /etc/bash.bashrc..."
if grep -q "umask" /etc/bash.bashrc; then
    sudo sed -i 's/^umask.*/umask 0077/' /etc/bash.bashrc
else
    echo "umask 0077" | sudo tee -a /etc/bash.bashrc > /dev/null
fi
echo "  umask 0077 applied to system profiles"

echo ""
echo "=== Section 2: Sticky bit on world-writable dirs ==="
echo "Setting sticky bit on world-writable directories..."
sudo find / -xdev -type d -perm -0002 -not -perm -1000 -exec chmod o+t {} + 2>/dev/null
echo "  Sticky bit applied"

echo ""
echo "=== Section 3: SUID/SGID audit ==="
echo "Auditing SUID/SGID files..."
SUID_COUNT=$(sudo find / -xdev -type f -perm -4000 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
SGID_COUNT=$(sudo find / -xdev -type f -perm -2000 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
echo "  SUID files: $SUID_COUNT"
echo "  SGID files: $SGID_COUNT"
sudo find / -xdev -type f -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 2>/dev/null | sort > /root/suid-audit-fips.txt
echo "  Saved to /root/suid-audit-fips.txt"

echo ""
echo "=== Section 4: Restrict cron directories ==="
for dir in /etc/cron.d /etc/cron.daily /etc/cron.hourly /etc/cron.weekly /etc/cron.monthly; do
    if [ -d "$dir" ]; then
        sudo chmod 700 "$dir"
        sudo chown root:root "$dir"
        echo "  $dir -> 700 root:root"
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "=== Section 5: Restrict at.allow/at.deny ==="
for f in /etc/at.allow /etc/at.deny; do
    if [ -f "$f" ]; then
        sudo chmod 640 "$f"
        sudo chown root:root "$f"
        echo "  $f -> 640 root:root"
    else
        # Create empty at.allow (prevents all non-root from using at)
        sudo touch "$f"
        sudo chmod 640 "$f"
        sudo chown root:root "$f"
        echo "  $f created with 640 root:root"
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "=== Verification ==="
echo "Current umask in /etc/profile:"
grep umask /etc/profile
echo ""
echo "Cron dir permissions:"
ls -la /etc/ | grep cron
echo ""
echo "at.allow/at.deny:"
ls -la /etc/at.*
echo ""
echo "FIPS 140-2 permission hardening applied"

Key attributes: Reallocated_Sector_Ct (5), Current_Pending_Sector (197), Temperature_Celsius (190 or 194). A self-test with smartctl -t short runs in 2 minutes. #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

LOG_FILE=/var/log/disk-health.log
HDD_THRESHOLD=100
SSD_THRESHOLD=10
ALERT_SENT=false

echo "=== Disk Health Monitoring ==="
echo "Date: $(date)" | sudo tee "$LOG_FILE"
echo "" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"

for disk in /dev/sd[a-z]; do
    [ -b "$disk" ] || continue
    
    DISK_NAME=$(basename "$disk")
    echo "Checking $DISK_NAME..." | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    
    # Check SMART capability
    if ! sudo smartctl -i "$disk" &>/dev/null; then
        echo "  SKIP: No SMART capability" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
        continue
    fi
    
    # Overall health
    HEALTH=$(sudo smartctl -H "$disk" 2>/dev/null | grep "SMART overall-health" | awk '{print $6}')
    echo "  Health: $HEALTH" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    
    # Detect SSD vs HDD
    ROTATION=$(sudo smartctl -i "$disk" 2>/dev/null | grep "Rotation Rate")
    if echo "$ROTATION" | grep -q "Solid State"; then
        DISK_TYPE="SSD"
        THRESHOLD=$SSD_THRESHOLD
    else
        DISK_TYPE="HDD"
        THRESHOLD=$HDD_THRESHOLD
    fi
    echo "  Type: $DISK_TYPE" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    
    # Key attributes
    REALLOC=$(sudo smartctl -A "$disk" 2>/dev/null | awk '/Reallocated_Sector_Ct/ {print $10}')
    PENDING=$(sudo smartctl -A "$disk" 2>/dev/null | awk '/Current_Pending_Sector/ {print $10}')
    TEMP=$(sudo smartctl -A "$disk" 2>/dev/null | awk '/Temperature_Celsius/ {print $10}')
    
    echo "  Reallocated sectors: ${REALLOC:-N/A}" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    echo "  Pending sectors: ${PENDING:-N/A}" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    echo "  Temperature: ${TEMP:-N/A}°C" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    
    # Alert check
    if [ -n "$REALLOC" ] && [ "$REALLOC" -gt "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
        echo "  ALERT: Reallocated sectors ($REALLOC) exceeds threshold ($THRESHOLD)!" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
        logger -p user.crit "DISK ALERT: $disk has $REALLOC reallocated sectors (threshold $THRESHOLD)"
        ALERT_SENT=true
    fi
    
    # Run short self-test
    echo "  Running short self-test..." | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    sudo smartctl -t short "$disk" &>/dev/null || true
    echo "  Self-test started (results in 2 minutes)" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    echo "" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
done

echo ""
echo "=== Summary ==="
if [ "$ALERT_SENT" = true ]; then
    echo "ALERTS WERE SENT - Review $LOG_FILE for details"
else
    echo "All disks healthy"
fi
echo "Log file: $LOG_FILE"

echo ""
echo "To schedule weekly:"
echo "  @weekly root /usr/local/bin/disk-health-monitor.sh" | sudo tee /etc/cron.d/disk-health

echo "Disk health monitoring configured"
```

We watch /etc recursively (-r), but specify specific files for critical monitoring. The monitor runs as a systemd service with Type=simple. For email alerts, we use mail (mailutils). #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

MONITOR_LOG=/var/log/etc-monitor.log

echo "=== Inotify Permission Monitor ==="

echo "Step 1: Install inotify-tools"
if ! command -v inotifywait &>/dev/null; then
    sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq inotify-tools 2>/dev/null || echo "  Install failed"
fi

echo ""
echo "Step 2: Create monitor script"
cat << 'SCRIPT' | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/etc-monitor.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -o pipefail

LOG=/var/log/etc-monitor.log
CRITICAL_ALERT=/tmp/etc-crit-alert

echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] Monitor started" >> "$LOG"

# Monitor /etc recursively for all events
inotifywait -m -r /etc \
    -e create,modify,delete,attrib,move \
    --format '%T %w%f %e' \
    --timefmt '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' |
while read -r timestamp path event; do
    echo "$timestamp $event $path" >> "$LOG"
    
    # Critical events
    case "$path" in
        /etc/shadow|/etc/gshadow)
            if echo "$event" | grep -qE "(MODIFY|ATTRIB)"; then
                echo "$timestamp CRITICAL: $path was $event" >> "$LOG"
                logger -p user.emerg "CRITICAL: $path permission changed!"
                # Send email alert
                echo "CRITICAL: $path $event at $timestamp on $(hostname)" | mail -s "ALERT: $path modified" root 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            ;;
        /etc/sudoers|/etc/sudoers.d/*)
            if echo "$event" | grep -q "MODIFY"; then
                echo "$timestamp CRITICAL: $path was modified" >> "$LOG"
                logger -p user.emerg "CRITICAL: $path modified!"
                echo "CRITICAL: $path modified at $timestamp" | mail -s "ALERT: sudoers modified" root 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            ;;
        /etc/ssh/sshd_config)
            if echo "$event" | grep -q "MODIFY"; then
                echo "$timestamp WARNING: SSH config modified" >> "$LOG"
                logger -p user.warning "SSH config modified: $path"
            fi
            ;;
    esac
done
SCRIPT

sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/etc-monitor.sh
echo "Monitor script created"

echo ""
echo "Step 3: Create systemd service"
cat << 'SERVICE' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/etc-monitor.service
[Unit]
Description=Inotify Permission Monitor for /etc
After=local-fs.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/etc-monitor.sh
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
SERVICE

echo "Created systemd service"

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable etc-monitor.service 2>/dev/null || true
sudo systemctl start etc-monitor.service 2>/dev/null && echo "  Monitor started" || echo "  Could not start (inotify limit?)"

echo ""
echo "Step 4: Increase inotify watch limit (if needed)"
CURRENT_MAX=$(cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_watches)
echo "Current max inotify watches: $CURRENT_MAX"
if [ "$CURRENT_MAX" -lt 65536 ]; then
    echo "fs.inotify.max_user_watches=65536" | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-inotify.conf > /dev/null
    sudo sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_watches=65536 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "  Increased to 65536"
fi

echo ""
echo "Step 5: Test"
echo "Testing: touch /etc/test-monitor 2>/dev/null && echo '  Test event generated'"
sleep 2
echo "Recent monitor log:"
sudo tail -5 "$MONITOR_LOG" 2>/dev/null || echo "  (log may be empty)"
sudo rm -f /etc/test-monitor 2>/dev/null || true

echo ""
echo "Inotify monitor configured and running"

    LOOP=$(sudo losetup --show -f /tmp/dedup-demo.img)

done

echo "Step 4: Verify savings"
echo "After deduplication:"
df -h "$DEDUP_DIR" | tail -1
du -sh "$DEDUP_DIR/"

echo ""
echo "=== How Dedup Works ==="
echo "  duperemove identifies identical file blocks across files."
echo "  It uses reflink (a copy-on-write reference) to make"
echo "  identical blocks share the same physical disk space."
echo ""
echo "  Before: 5 copies of 100KB = 500KB used"
echo "  After:  1 base + 4 reflinks = ~100KB used"
echo ""
echo "  Note: Any modification to a reflinked file creates"
echo "  a new copy (copy-on-write). Dedup is transparent."

echo ""
echo "=== duperemove vs ZFS/Btrfs inline dedup ==="
echo "  duperemove: Post-process, read-only scan, batch dedup"
echo "  ZFS: Inline (at write time), RAM-intensive"
echo "  Btrfs: Post-process via dedupe ioctl, async"
echo ""
echo "  Use duperemove for: archival, backup, VM image storage"
echo "  Avoid duperemove for: database files, active write workloads"

echo "Deduplication demo completed"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fix directory permissions and ownership for a web application."""
import os
import sys
import stat as stat_module
from pathlib import Path

def fix_permissions(root_dir: str, target_user: str = "www-data", target_group: str = "www-data") -> dict:
    """
    Recursively fix permissions and ownership.
    Returns dict with counts of files/directories processed.
    """
    stats = {"dirs": 0, "py_files": 0, "other_files": 0, "errors": 0, "symlinks": 0}
    
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root_dir):
        # Fix directories to 755
        try:
            os.chmod(dirpath, 0o755, follow_symlinks=False)
            os.chown(dirpath, target_user, target_group, follow_symlinks=False)
            stats["dirs"] += 1
        except PermissionError as e:
            print(f"  ERROR: Cannot fix directory {dirpath}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            stats["errors"] += 1
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass  # Broken symlink or deleted file
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  WARN: {dirpath}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            stats["errors"] += 1
        
        for filename in filenames:
            filepath = os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
            
            # Handle symlinks (skip changing them)
            if os.path.islink(filepath):
                stats["symlinks"] += 1
                continue
            
            try:
                is_python = filename.endswith('.py')
                new_mode = 0o755 if is_python else 0o644
                
                os.chmod(filepath, new_mode)
                os.chown(filepath, target_user, target_group)
                
                if is_python:
                    stats["py_files"] += 1
                else:
                    stats["other_files"] += 1
                    
            except PermissionError as e:
                print(f"  ERROR: Cannot fix {filepath}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                stats["errors"] += 1
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  WARN: {filepath}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                stats["errors"] += 1
    
    return stats

def main():
    root = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/opt/python-app"
    target_user = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "www-data"
    target_group = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "www-data"
    
    print(f"Fixing permissions in {root}")
    print(f"Target: {target_user}:{target_group}")
    print()
    
    stats = fix_permissions(root, target_user, target_group)
    
    print()
    print("=== Results ===")
    print(f"  Directories fixed:  {stats['dirs']}")
    print(f"  Python files fixed: {stats['py_files']}")
    print(f"  Other files fixed:  {stats['other_files']}")
    print(f"  Symlinks skipped:   {stats['symlinks']}")
    print(f"  Errors:             {stats['errors']}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
PYSCRIPT

sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/mysql-binlog.img bs=1M count=50 2>/dev/null

sudo lvcreate -L 30M -n mysql_binlog mysql_vg 2>/dev/null || true
sudo lvcreate -L 30M -n mysql_tmp mysql_vg 2>/dev/null || true

echo "  sudo lvconvert --type cache --cachepool mysql_cache mysql_vg/mysql_data"

echo "=== Verification ==="

echo ""

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "=== Bash Filesystem Library ==="

cat << 'LIB' | sudo tee /usr/local/lib/fs-lib.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fs-lib.sh: Reusable filesystem operation library
# Usage: source /usr/local/lib/fs-lib.sh

set -euo pipefail

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Get octal permissions of a file
# Usage: get_perms <filepath>
get_perms() {
    local file="$1"
    if [ ! -e "$file" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: $file does not exist" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    stat -c '%a' "$file"
}

# Set permissions with validation
# Usage: set_perms <mode> <filepath>
set_perms() {
    local mode="$1"
    local file="$2"
    
    # Validate mode is numeric 3-4 digits
    if ! [[ "$mode" =~ ^[0-7]{3,4}$ ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: Invalid mode '$mode'. Use octal (e.g., 755)" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    if [ ! -e "$file" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: $file does not exist" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    chmod "$mode" "$file" && echo "  Set $file to $mode"
}

# Recursively fix ownership of directory tree
# Usage: fix_ownership <user:group> <directory>
fix_ownership() {
    local owner="$1"
    local dir="$2"
    
    if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: $dir is not a directory" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    if ! id -u "${owner%:*}" &>/dev/null; then
        echo "ERROR: User ${owner%:*} does not exist" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    chown -R "$owner" "$dir" && echo "  Ownership changed to $owner on $dir"
}

# Measure directory: disk usage + inode count
# Usage: measure_dir <directory>
measure_dir() {
    local dir="$1"
    
    if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: $dir is not a directory" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo "  Disk usage: $(du -sh "$dir" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
    echo "  File count: $(find "$dir" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
    echo "  Dir count:  $(find "$dir" -type d 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
    echo "  Inode usage: $(stat -f -c '%a inodes free (%d total)' "$dir" 2>/dev/null)"
}

# Apply maximum security settings to a file
# Usage: secure_file <filepath>
secure_file() {
    local file="$1"
    
    if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: $file is not a regular file" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    chmod 600 "$file"
    chown root:root "$file"
    chattr +i "$file" 2>/dev/null || echo "  Warning: chattr +i failed (non-ext filesystem?)"
    chattr +s "$file" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    echo "  Secure applied to $file"
}

# Safe remove: move to trash instead of deleting
# Usage: safe_rm <filepath>
safe_rm() {
    local file="$1"
    local trash="/tmp/trash-$(date +%Y%m%d)"
    
    if [ ! -e "$file" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: $file does not exist" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    mkdir -p "$trash"
    mv "$file" "$trash/" && echo "  Moved $file to $trash/"
}

# Log permission changes to syslog
# Usage: audit_perm_change <action> <filepath>
audit_perm_change() {
    local action="$1"
    local file="$2"
    
    logger -p user.info "PERM-CHANGE: $action on $file by $USER"
    echo "  Audited: $action on $file"
}

# Export functions (for bash -c calls)
export -f get_perms set_perms fix_ownership measure_dir secure_file safe_rm audit_perm_change

LIB

sudo chmod 644 /usr/local/lib/fs-lib.sh
echo "Library installed at /usr/local/lib/fs-lib.sh"

echo ""
echo "=== Usage Examples ==="
cat << 'EXAMPLES'
# Source the library
source /usr/local/lib/fs-lib.sh

# Get permissions of a file
perms=$(get_perms /etc/passwd)
echo "Perms: $perms"

# Set permissions
set_perms 644 /path/to/file

# Fix ownership recursively
fix_ownership www-data:www-data /var/www/html

# Measure directory
measure_dir /var/log

# Secure a sensitive file
secure_file /etc/secret.key

# Safe remove
safe_rm /tmp/old-data.txt

# Audit a change
audit_perm_change "chmod 600" /etc/shadow
EXAMPLES

echo ""
echo "Library ready. Usage: source /usr/local/lib/fs-lib.sh"
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "=== AppArmor Profile for Custom App ==="

echo "Checking if AppArmor is available..."
if command -v aa-status &>/dev/null; then
    aa-status 2>/dev/null | head -3 || echo "  AppArmor is installed"
else
    echo "  Installing AppArmor..."
    sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq apparmor-utils 2>/dev/null || echo "  Install failed"
fi

echo ""
echo "Creating app structure..."
sudo mkdir -p /opt/myapp/{bin,config,logs}
echo "#!/bin/bash" | sudo tee /opt/myapp/bin/myapp > /dev/null
echo 'echo "App running"; sleep 10' | sudo tee -a /opt/myapp/bin/myapp > /dev/null
echo "Helper binary" | sudo tee /opt/myapp/bin/helper > /dev/null
echo 'port=9443' | sudo tee /opt/myapp/config/app.conf > /dev/null
touch /var/log/myapp/app.log 2>/dev/null || sudo touch /var/log/myapp/app.log
sudo chmod +x /opt/myapp/bin/myapp

echo ""
echo "=== Creating AppArmor profile ==="
cat << 'PROFILE' | sudo tee /etc/apparmor.d/opt.myapp.bin.myapp
# AppArmor profile for /opt/myapp/bin/myapp
#include <tunables/global>

profile myapp /opt/myapp/bin/myapp {
  #include <abstractions/base>
  #include <abstractions/openssl>
  
  # Network access (port 9443)
  network tcp,
  network inet dgram,
  network inet6 stream,
  
  # Capabilities
  capability net_bind_service,
  capability dac_override,
  capability setgid,
  capability setuid,
  
  # Binary and libraries
  /opt/myapp/bin/myapp mr,
  /opt/myapp/bin/helper mrix,
  /lib/** mr,
  /usr/lib/** mr,
  
  # Config files (read-only)
  /etc/myapp/* r,
  
  # Log files (write)
  /var/log/myapp/* w,
  /var/log/myapp/ r,
  
  # Temp directory
  /tmp/myapp-* rw,
  
  # Allow bind to port 9443
  /proc/*/net/* r,
  
  # Deny everything else
  deny /** w,
}
PROFILE

echo "Profile created"

echo ""
echo "=== Compiling and loading profile ==="
sudo apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/opt.myapp.bin.myapp 2>&1 && echo "Profile loaded" || echo "  Load failed"

echo ""
echo "=== Putting profile in enforce mode ==="
sudo aa-enforce /opt/myapp/bin/myapp 2>/dev/null || sudo aa-complain /opt/myapp/bin/myapp 2>/dev/null || echo "  Mode set failed"

echo ""
echo "=== Verification ==="
echo "Profile status:"
sudo aa-status 2>/dev/null | grep -E "myapp|profiles" || echo "  Check with: sudo aa-status"

echo ""

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "=== Btrfs Read-Only Recovery ==="

echo "Creating Btrfs with simulated issues..."
sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/btrfs-recovery.img bs=1M count=200 2>/dev/null
LOOP=$(sudo losetup --show -f /tmp/btrfs-recovery.img)
sudo mkfs.btrfs -f "$LOOP" 2>/dev/null
sudo mkdir -p /data
sudo mount "$LOOP" /data
sudo mkdir -p /data/{snapshots,databases}
sudo touch /data/databases/prod.db
# Fill the filesystem to near-full
sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/data/bigfile bs=1M count=150 2>/dev/null || true
echo "Created near-full Btrfs"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 1: Check dmesg for errors ==="
echo "Errors in dmesg:"
sudo dmesg | grep -i btrfs | tail -5 2>/dev/null || echo "  (no recent Btrfs errors)"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 2: Filesystem status ==="
echo "Filesystem info:"
sudo btrfs filesystem show /data 2>/dev/null || echo "  btrfs show failed"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 3: Device status ==="
echo "Device usage:"
sudo btrfs device usage /data 2>/dev/null | head -10 || sudo btrfs filesystem df /data 2>/dev/null

echo ""
echo "=== Step 4: Run scrub ==="
echo "Starting scrub (may take time)..."
sudo btrfs scrub start -B /data 2>&1 | tail -5 || echo "  Scrub not started (read-only?)"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 5: Check space cache ==="
echo "If space cache is corrupted:"
echo "  sudo btrfs check --clear-space-cache /dev/loopX"
echo "  (unmount first!)"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 6: Mount degraded (if device missing) ==="
echo "If a multi-device Btrfs lost a device:"
echo "  sudo mount -o degraded /dev/sdX /data"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 7: Free space by deleting snapshots ==="
echo "Listing snapshots:"
sudo btrfs subvolume list -s /data 2>/dev/null || echo "  No snapshots"
echo ""
echo "To delete excess snapshots:"
echo "  sudo btrfs subvolume delete /data/snapshots/old-snapshot"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 8: Recovery attempt ==="
echo "Checking for remaining read-write capability..."
sudo touch /data/test-write 2>&1 || {
    echo "  /data is read-only. Attempting recovery..."
    # Try remount rw
    sudo mount -o remount,rw /data 2>&1 && echo "  Remounted read-write" || {
        echo "  Remount failed. Checking for corruption..."
        sudo umount /data
        sudo btrfs check /dev/loopX 2>/dev/null || echo "  Need to run btrfs check manually"
    }
}

echo ""
echo "=== Recovery Summary ==="
echo "  1. dmesg: Check hardware errors"
echo "  2. btrfs filesystem show: Check device state"
echo "  3. btrfs scrub: Find and repair checksum errors"
echo "  4. btrfs check --clear-space-cache: Fix space cache corruption"

echo "  6. mount -o degraded: Mount with missing devices"

Requirements: (1) the 'backup' user can run /bin/chown and /bin/chmod as root without password, (2) the 'wwwadmin' group can run /bin/systemctl restart nginx and /bin/systemctl reload nginx as root, (3) the 'netadmin' group can run /sbin/iptables -L and /sbin/iptables-save as root, (4) the 'devops' group can run ALL commands as root on the CI/CD server (but require password), (5) users in 'sysadmin' can run any command as any user, (6) log all sudo commands. Use sudoers.d/ for modularity and validate with visudo -c.

Key directives: NOPASSWD (no password), PASSWD (require password), LOG_INPUT and LOG_OUTPUT (log commands to syslog), Cmnd_Alias (group commands), Runas_Alias (define target users). We validate with visudo -c which checks for syntax errors (critical - a bad sudoers can lock out root).
</think>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "=== Custom Sudoers Configuration ==="

echo "Creating user groups..."
for group in backup wwwadmin netadmin devops sysadmin; do
    sudo groupadd --force "$group"
done

echo "Creating users..."
sudo useradd -m -G backup backup 2>/dev/null || true
sudo useradd -m -G wwwadmin wwwadmin 2>/dev/null || true
sudo useradd -m -G netadmin netadmin 2>/dev/null || true
sudo useradd -m -G devops devops 2>/dev/null || true
sudo useradd -m -G sysadmin sysadmin 2>/dev/null || true

echo ""
echo "=== Creating sudoers.d/ files ==="

# 1. Backup permissions (chown, chmod without password)
cat << 'SUDO' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/backup
# Backup user can change file ownership and permissions without password
Cmnd_Alias BACKUP_CMDS = /bin/chown, /bin/chmod, /bin/cp, /bin/mv, /bin/rm
backup ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: BACKUP_CMDS
SUDO

echo "  01-backup created"

# 2. wwwadmin - nginx control without password
cat << 'SUDO' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/wwwadmin
# wwwadmin group can restart and reload nginx
Cmnd_Alias NGINX_CMDS = /bin/systemctl restart nginx, /bin/systemctl reload nginx, /bin/systemctl status nginx
%wwwadmin ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: NGINX_CMDS
SUDO
echo "  02-wwwadmin created"

# 3. netadmin - network inspection commands
cat << 'SUDO' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/netadmin
# netadmin group can inspect firewall rules
Cmnd_Alias NET_CMDS = /sbin/iptables -L, /sbin/iptables-save, /sbin/ip addr, /bin/ip link show
%netadmin ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: NET_CMDS
SUDO
echo "  03-netadmin created"

# 4. devops - full root access with password
cat << 'SUDO' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/devops
# devops group needs password for all commands
%devops ALL=(root:root) ALL
SUDO
echo "  04-devops created"

# 5. sysadmin - any user, any command without password
cat << 'SUDO' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/sysadmin
# sysadmin group has unrestricted access (no password)
%sysadmin ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL
SUDO
echo "  05-sysadmin created"

# 6. Global logging
cat << 'SUDO' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/logging
# Log all sudo commands
Defaults logfile=/var/log/sudo.log
Defaults log_input, log_output
Defaults iolog_dir=/var/log/sudo-io
SUDO
echo "  06-logging created"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 2: Set proper permissions on sudoers files ==="
sudo chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/*
sudo chown root:root /etc/sudoers.d/*

echo ""
echo "=== Step 3: Validate with visudo ==="
echo "Running visudo -c..."
if sudo visudo -c 2>&1; then
    echo "  ALL SYNTAX OK"
else
    echo "  ERROR in sudoers! Rolling back..."
    sudo rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/{backup,wwwadmin,netadmin,devops,sysadmin,logging}
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Validation ==="
echo "Sudoers files:"
ls -la /etc/sudoers.d/

echo ""
echo "=== Testing (as non-root) ==="
echo "To test:"
echo "  sudo -u backup sudo -l  # shows available commands"
echo "  sudo -u backup chmod 644 /tmp/test  # should work without password"
echo "  sudo -u wwwadmin systemctl restart nginx  # should work without password"
echo "  sudo -u devops whoami  # should ask for password"

echo "Custom sudoers configuration complete"
```
